title: Close posts the parts cost to the mapped account with its source
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, whose default internal category is General Internal.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. Open Accounting > Journal Entries.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 4:

  • An entry dated the posting date debits 6500 Vehicle Expenses (General Internal's starting account) $80.00 and credits Inventory $80.00, with the source "Internal work order", linked to the Closed record.
  • No revenue, receivable or tax is posted for it.
  • The entry date is the posting date at the location, not the day before.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

  • S8-R2: “At Close, the hub posts the parts cost entries dated the posting date: debit the mapped expense account, credit Inventory, for the cost of the stock parts, source "Internal work order" (or "No-charge work order"), linked to the record of S8-R1.”
  • S8-R1: “At Close, the hub receives the invoice event carrying the classification (Internal or No Charge), the category, the original work order and line and the original technician when set, the work order number and the asset, and keeps an invoice record with a status Closed (new in the hub), the badge, "No Charge" in place of a total, and no payment tabs. It posts no revenue, no receivable and no tax for it. The record's page (Accounting > Sales > Invoices) shows the header with the existing link to the work order in ShopView, a summary (number, customer, asset, classification, category, original work order when set, posting date, "No Charge", and the posted Parts cost and Shop supplies totals) and the journal entry section with the entries of S8-R2 and S8-R3; no lines (they are on the NO CHARGE document), no payment, credit memo or write-off tabs and no Void (Reopen is done in ShopView, Story 4).”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 4848 (TP-631): “inside the posting date's local day at the location.”
  • Tech plan line 4848 (TP-631): “The hub converts instants to the location's day, so UTC midnight of a US location's date would land on the previous day.”
